title: Old Testament Survey
description: A guided tour of the Old Testament: its structure, storyline, major themes and theology. Students trace the history of Israel from creation and the patriarchs through exodus, conquest, monarchy, exile and return, and read representative texts from the Law, the Historical Books, Wisdom and Poetry, and the Prophets. The course emphasizes covenant, kingdom, and promise, and how the Old Testament prepares for and points to Jesus Christ.

quiz_bank.question: Why is Isaiah 52:13-53:12 central to the New Testament's understanding of Jesus' death?
quiz_bank.answer_key: It portrays a righteous servant who suffers and dies for others' sins, bears their iniquity, makes many righteous and is exalted; the NT quotes it repeatedly (Acts 8; 1 Pet 2:22-25; Mark 10:45) to explain the cross as substitutionary atonement.

lessons.paper_prompt: Write a 1,500-2,000 word paper tracing ONE theme through the Old Testament (for example covenant, kingship, the presence of God/temple, or the land) from its beginning to its expected fulfilment, showing how it is developed in the Law, the Historical Books, the Writings and the Prophets, and how the New Testament presents its fulfilment in Christ. Use at least three scripture passages from different sections of the Old Testament and at least two library sources, cited as (Author, Title, section).
